title: World editor
hypothesis: A minimal in-runtime editor — palette from the asset registry, plane placement, transform keys, JSON persistence and an edit/play toggle with live creature behaviors — is enough for a designer to build, save and playtest V2 world layouts without touching code.
success_signals: A layout built in the editor survives serialize -> reload -> load byte-identically.
Play mode drops the third-person player into the built world and every placed behavior runs.
Placed zhalm nodes form a working sound network without any code changes.
A designer can go from empty ground to a playable encounter in under ten minutes.
kill_criteria: Placement/selection is too imprecise to position assets deliberately.
Mode switching corrupts world state or the player rig.
Behavior updates make editing sluggish below usable frame rates.
reset_strategy: Editor mode: clear all placed entities and reload the last loaded layout. Play mode: return creatures to their placement homes, reset the sound network and teleport the player to the world spawn. No backend state involved.
